newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of NAPM.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of NAPM.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Tuesday in moderate trade with most traders sidelined ahead of the U.S. June National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index and the outcome of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, dealers said.
The NAPM index for June is forecast to show a reading of 56.4 compared with a reading of 57.1 reported in May.

"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning on some position adjustments. Some traders were waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the the NAPM index," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact unless the index is way off market expectations. The market is also waiting for the outcome of the two-day FOMC meeting which starts today," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday and Wednesday/ Thursday rose 1/8 percentage point each to a common 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent. Week-fixed eased 1/16 point to 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Monday's 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, nine-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/16 5-15/16 and twelve-months was unchanged at 6-1/8 6 percent. -- P.Theseira (65-870-3085)
